movement_source: row 'Net profit after tax from continuing operations ("cash basis")', column 31 Dec 24 $M (cash basis) -> column 31 Dec 25 $M (cash basis)
headline: CBA's cash NPAT from continuing operations rose $313m or 6% to $5,445m in 1H26 from $5,132m in 1H25 (ev-18, ev-16, ev-63). The bank's own summary: total operating income $15,021m, up 7% (6.6% on the slide) from $14,097m; operating performance (income less operating expenses, pre-impairment) $8,131m, up 5% (5.3%) from $7,725m; loan impairment expense essentially flat at $319m (ev-9, ev-12, ev-53, ev-55, ev-13). Statutory NPAT including discontinued operations rose $233m or 5% to $5,367m, and statutory NPAT from continuing operations rose $270m or 5% to $5,412m — below the cash growth because of non-cash items: losses on acquisition/disposal/closure of businesses of $63m in 1H26 versus nil, hedging and IFRS volatility of $(15)m versus $1m, plus a $(45)m discontinued-operations loss (ev-19, ev-6, ev-4, ev-5, ev-61, ev-62). ROE (cash) rose 10bpts to 13.8% (ev-25). Income growth outpaced a 5% underlying cost rise, but $170m of notable items (nil in 1H25) and $94m more tax absorbed part of the gain.

drivers.narrative: NII rose $761m or 6% to $12,695m, "driven by a $96 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,232 billion, partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.04%". Average lending assets +$61bn or 7%: home loans +$31bn or 5% to $622bn, business/corporate +$29bn or 11% to $293bn.

Volume was the positive leg: AIEA +$96bn or 8% to $1,232bn, average lending +$61bn or 7% "due to growth in home, business and institutional lending"; liquid assets +$20bn or 12% to $189bn. The bank does not split the $761m NII movement into dollar volume and margin effects, so no dollar contribution is claimed here.

drivers.columns: Dec 24 Half to Dec 25 Half (NIM walk, bps)
drivers.narrative: NIM fell 4bps from 2.08% to 2.04%; excluding liquids, which have "broadly neutral impacts on net interest income", it fell only 1bp and the underlying NIM was unchanged. The primary NIM walk: liquids -3, asset pricing -2, funding costs -3, portfolio mix +1, basis risk 0, capital/replicating & other +6, Treasury & Markets -3 bps. No dollar value is published.

Up $163m or 8% to $2,326m. Trading income +$84m or 16% to $603m on higher Markets trading gains and favourable derivative valuation adjustments; commissions +$61m or 6% to $1,146m on higher insurance income including a CommInsure General Insurance sale milestone payment and equities volumes; lending fees +$16m to $465m; funds management +$7m to $67m; other income -$5m to $45m.

UNDERLYING (excludes notable items) opex rose $348m or 5% to $6,720m. The bank's primary walk: inflation +$275m, investment in technology +$222m, investment in frontline and operations +$78m, other -$6m, productivity -$221m. Staff +$169m to $4,139m (wage inflation, average FTE +2,448 to 51,755); IT services +$134m or 11% to $1,321m (cloud, licensing, AI); other +$40m; occupancy +$5m.

A $170m charge in 1H26 against nil in 1H25, so the full $170m is an adverse delta. It "relates to provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in NZ; an additional goodwill payment made to certain customers as a result of ASIC's Better Banking review; and domestic customer remediation". Including it, headline total opex rose 8% to $6,890m versus 5% underlying.

Essentially flat: LIE "decreased $1 million", $319m versus $320m (-0.3%), "primarily driven by improvements in business credit quality and easing conditions for households, partly offset by elevated geopolitical tensions and global macroeconomic uncertainty". Home loan 90+ day arrears 0.63%, down 7bps on the prior half; total provisions to credit RWA 1.55%.

Corporate tax expense was $2,367m, "an increase of $94 million or 4% on the prior comparative period, reflecting a 30.3% effective tax rate" — a negative contribution as tax rose with pre-tax profit. The effective tax rate fell 40bpts from 30.7% to 30.3%, "primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses", so tax grew more slowly (4%) than pre-tax profit (5%).

notable_items: 1H26 restructuring and notable items of $170m: provisions for settlement of legal proceedings in NZ; additional goodwill payment to customers from ASIC's Better Banking review; domestic customer remediation (ev-11, ev-15). 1H25 comparative was nil, so the whole $170m is an adverse year-on-year delta.

Statutory-to-cash non-cash items (NOT bridge drivers): loss on acquisition, disposal, closure and demerger of businesses $(63)m in 1H26 vs nil in 1H25; hedging and IFRS volatility $(15)m vs $1m; discontinued operations non-cash items $(45)m (ev-4, ev-5, ev-61, ev-62).

disagreements.explanation: The results book prints the growth rounded to a whole 6% (ev-16, ev-18) while the slide prints 6.1% (ev-57). Both derive from the same $5,132m to $5,445m movement; the difference is rounding only.
Results book rounds 924/14,097 to 7% (ev-9, ev-18); the slide prints 6.6% (ev-53). Same underlying $15,021m vs $14,097m levels, so rounding alone. Underlying opex likewise 5% vs 5.5%.

The Group Performance Summary prints $5,132m for continuing operations and $5,133m including the $1m of discontinued operations (ev-16, ev-3). The task bridge is built on the continuing-operations basis used by every component note, giving a $313m movement rather than $312m.

limitations: The bank publishes no single cash-NPAT waterfall in dollars for 1H26 vs 1H25; the bridge here is assembled from the Group Performance Summary rows plus each component note's own stated 'on the prior comparative period' movement. The components sum exactly to the $313m movement, leaving zero residual.

NII is claimed as a single $761m total. CBA does not publish a dollar split of NII into volume and margin effects, so nii.volume and nii.margin carry no contribution — only the AIEA (+$96bn, +8%) and NIM (-4bps) statements and the bps NIM walk.

The NIM walk bars are in basis points, not dollars, and cannot be converted to a dollar contribution; they explain the margin leg inside the $761m NII figure and must not be added to the dollar bridge.

CBA qualifies the liquids leg: growth in liquid assets has 'broadly neutral impacts on net interest income', so the -3bps liquids bar and the -4bps headline NIM overstate the economic margin pressure; the underlying NIM excluding liquids and institutional repos was unchanged, down just 1bp on the reported measure.

The underlying opex walk bars (inflation +275, technology +222, frontline +78, other -6, productivity -221) are gross legs inside the net $348m: the $221m productivity benefit offsets much of the gross investment, and the bank repeatedly notes increases were 'partly offset by productivity initiatives'.

Operating expenses are stated on the UNDERLYING basis ($6,720m, +$348m, excluding notable items); the headline total opex movement was +$518m (+8%) to $6,890m once the $170m of notable items is included.

The tax contribution is a mechanical consequence of higher pre-tax profit rather than an independent driver; the effective tax rate actually fell 40bpts to 30.3%, a modest favourable offset the bridge does not isolate.
Divisional cash NPAT movements (Business Banking +14% to $2,272m, RBS +1% to $2,727m) are not reconciled to the Group component bridge here; no divisional attribution is claimed.
Comparative information has been restated to conform to current-period presentation, per the Group Performance Summary footnote.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.

Cash net profit after tax (“cash NPAT” or “cash profit”) from continuing operations increased $313 million or 6% on the prior comparative period to $5,445 million. The result was driven by a 7% increase in operating income, a 5% increase in operating expenses 2, and a $1 million decrease in loan impairment expense.

numbers.label: Cash NPAT increase Dec25 vs Dec24

evidence_records.quote: The Bank’s statutory net profit after tax (NPAT) from continuing operations for the half year ended 31 December 2025 increased $270 million or 5% on the prior comparative period to $5,412 million. The Bank’s statutory NPAT (including discontinued operations) increased $233 million or 5% on the prior comparative period to $5,367 million.

Net Interest Income (NII) increased 6%, primarily driven by a $96 billion or 8% increase in Average Interest Earning Assets (AIEA), partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in Net Interest Margin (NIM). Excluding the impact of liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, the underlying NIM was unchanged.

Average lending assets increased by $61 billion or 7% due to growth in home, business and institutional lending. Underlying NIM was primarily driven by higher earnings from the replicating portfolio and equity hedges, and favourable funding mix from strong growth in at-call deposits, offset by Treasury and Markets, the impact of declining interest rates, and increased deposit and lending price competition.

Other operating income increased 8% with higher trading income from Markets including favourable derivative valuation adjustments, growth in equities volumes, higher insurance income including a milestone payment recognised in relation to the sale of Commonwealth Insurance Limited (CommInsure General Insurance), and higher syndication and institutional lending fee income, partly offset by lower Structured Asset Finance revenue following the sale of the aircraft lease portfolio, and lower Treasury income from liquid asset sales.

Operating expenses 2 increased 5%, mainly driven by higher staff expenses due to inflation and an increase in full-time equivalent staff (FTE), and additional technology spend to support investment in infrastructure, resilience and AI capabilities, as well as higher cloud computing volumes and software licensing, partly offset by productivity initiatives.

Loan impairment expense (LIE) decreased $1 million, primarily driven by improvements in business credit quality and easing conditions for households, partly offset by elevated geopolitical tensions and global macroeconomic uncertainty.
Return on equity (“cash basis”) increased 10 basis points to 13.8% due to higher cash NPAT being partly offset by higher net assets.
Other operating income was $2,326 million, an increase of $163 million or 8% on the prior comparative period.

numbers.label: Other operating income increase Dec25 vs Dec24

evidence_records.quote: Commissions increased by $61 million or 6% to $1,146 million, mainly driven by higher insurance income, including a milestone payment recognised in relation to the sale of Commonwealth Insurance Limited (CommInsure General Insurance), and higher equities income due to growth in trading volumes, partly offset by lower deposit fees mainly due to fee waivers, and the sale of the private advice business.
Lending fees increased by $16 million or 4% to $465 million, mainly due to higher volume driven bank guarantees and higher syndication and institutional lending fee income.

Trading income increased by $84 million or 16% to $603 million, mainly driven by higher trading gains in Markets and favourable derivative valuation adjustments, partly offset by lower Treasury income from liquid asset sales and lower sales volume in foreign exchange.
Funds management income increased by $7 million or 12% to $67 million, from higher average net flows and favourable market performance in New Zealand.

Other income decreased by $5 million or 10% to $45 million, mainly driven by lower Structured Asset Finance revenue from the sale of the aircraft lease portfolio, and lower earnings from minority investments, partly offset by a fair value gain on our investment in Gemini following its Initial Public Offering.
